abstract.text: Inherited from
The status card’s title: the Mac’s name while its helper is connected or names the
Bluetooth host, “Your Mac” while a way to one that hasn’t said works, and “Not connected”
while none does.
The Sound row’s value: whether the Mac’s sound plays here.
The capture devices currently plugged in.
Keyboard’s shortcuts, while open.
The computers proven to use this device as their Bluetooth keyboard, and listeners without proof.
The Bluetooth devices using this device as their keyboard, named from the paired Macs by
their helper’s fingerprint; none while the link isn’t up.
The pixel format automatic picks at the resolution and frame rate in effect.
The format chosen for the card whose formats are loaded, as its profile keeps it, or
for Automatic.
The input method on over the Mac’s reported layout, such as Telex, which rewrites what
Bluetooth types;
while keys type as the layout says.
The Input row’s value: how touch works.
The formats of the selected device, as far as they have loaded.
Keyboard’s custom keys, while open.
Whether this display folds, which adds a scaling for the folded stream pane.
The device being captured from: the chosen one when plugged in, else the first.
What the Mac display choice does now.
The keyboard shortcuts, for the count on Keyboard’s row.
The pixel formats the device offers at the resolution and frame rate in effect, best first.
The “Glance at your Mac” rows.
The tips under About.
The resolutions the selected device offers, each with its frame rates.
The layout the helper reported for the Mac, else the one picked here, else the one
matching this device’s language; chosen as Bluetooth chooses it.
The Sound rows and Advanced’s Sound timing.
The settings sheet: capture device and format, display scaling, the Mac to send input to, and input preferences.
The stream’s level as the connected helper last reported it.
The keyboard layouts the helpers reported, which Bluetooth types through ahead of the pick.
Whether the Mac display rows show: hidden only when the App Store helper can’t extend and
the person turned off the rows for what needs the Direct download.
What Bluetooth types and gestures through for the computers using this device as their
keyboard: the first one a paired Mac’s helper names, by what that Mac’s helper said; else,
for a computer no helper names, the layout picked for it here, with nothing reported, so a
Mac without the helper doesn’t type through another Mac’s layout; else the last reporting
Mac’s.
The layout picked for the computer Bluetooth types to, else the one picked here, else
while nobody picked one.
The Mac’s own three-finger drag as its helper last reported it, else the switch here.
The Picture in Picture row.
The resolution and frame rate in effect, with the pixel format chosen for them or
for automatic.
What the Mac Bluetooth types to said, while this device still holds its pairing, as
finds it.
The layout matching this device’s language, which stands in while none is picked.
The iPad and iPhone app: one screen that shows the Mac’s picture and sends the Mac input from touch, trackpad, mouse, Pencil, and keyboard.
The format in effect: the chosen one when the device can do it, else the device’s preferred,
its own mode first, as the capture session resolves it.
The helper stream’s frame size while its picture is on screen, which the upscalers are for then.
Headwire Pro under About, and the switch that hides its locked features.
The upscaler the picker shows: the stored pick when it is offered, else what runs instead.
The Video, Input and Instant switch rows.
The frame rates offered at the selected resolution, highest first.
The device the person chose.
The Picture row’s value: the format in effect, such as “1920 × 1080 · 60 fps”, or the
scaling while no card’s formats are loaded.
What Automatic picks, the card’s own mode first, marked as recommended in the pickers.
The capture cards under Advanced.
The selection with the chosen pixel format carried over where the device offers it there, else automatic.
The chosen pixel format when the format in effect uses it, else
for automatic.
The screens pushed over the top level, outermost first; empty at the top level.
The Bluetooth row’s value: the chosen Mac’s name, “Keyboard connected” when it can’t be
named, “Choose your Mac” while devices are connected and none is chosen, or the link’s state.
Whether input is reaching a Mac.
The upscalers this device runs on the picture on screen, Off first.
How input is sent to the Mac.
How the stream is drawn.
Share usage data and Send feedback, under About.
The status card’s line: how the Mac is connected, in a few words, such as “USB cable” or
“Capture card · Bluetooth”, each way that doesn’t work now saying so, as the status line
does. What doesn’t work is What works now’s and Connection’s to explain.
